comparator.name: Arts and Culture Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The exact Dutch-taught target is retained. Current official year pages explicitly describe first year 2027–2028, second year 2028–2029 and third year 2029–2030. Together they establish one coherent indicative incoming 2027 pathway:60 EC first year,30 EC second-year major plus two 15 EC Faculty of Artsminors, then 30 EC third-year major/thesis plus 30 EC free space. The standard domestic third year is selected by the neutral curriculum-order rule; it requires Popular Music and Society, Visual Culture, Spatial Culture, Working in the Cultural Field and a 10 EC thesis. These webpages identify the compulsory and choice allocations and total 180 EC without mixing entrant cohorts. The 2026–2027 OER was inspected for current academic aims and progression, not falsely applied as the legal 2027 entrant curriculum; its B 2/B 3 tables explicitly concern earlier cohorts. Known current prerequisites are satisfied by the order of the indicative plan: Cultural Theory beforeSpatial Culture, Analyse van Beeld beforeVisual Culture, compulsory B 2 major beforethesis. The official prospective pages state that this future offer is indicative and may change; the comparison is a planning aid, not a guarantee of future regulations or course availability.

alternatives.concept: A broad arts-and-culture route combining art history and heritage, literature, film and media with stylistics, social theory, ethics and qualitative inquiry. Historiography examines how art is interpreted; the historical research seminar studies a fixed military-history case rather than a freely chosen cultural-studies thesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three provisional concepts remain supported by exact-target interests and actual UCR content: broad arts/media/cultural analysis; culture, identity and power; literature, film and communication. Three institutional-politics courses in the second route are replaced with art history, stylistics and film adaptation to give cultural objects adequate weight. Performance/music/festival interests remain evidenced but cannot produce an additional included route under the three-alternative maximum, and UCR lacks the dedicated music and performing-arts sequence. These concepts respond to the defining arts-and-cultural-interpretation substance of the official indicative 2027 intake pathway; specialist music, performance, festival and thesis gaps remain explicit.

notes.text: The UCR programmes offer substantial art history, literature, film, media and cultural interpretation. Radboud also requires music analysis, opera and musical theatre, performance culture, festival work and a separate bachelor thesis. UCR does not reproduce these specialist sequences. Its creative laboratory excludes music performance, and its history seminar studies the 1809 Walcheren Expedition.

audience.programmeDescription: The Dutch-taught Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen route studies visual art, literature, music, film, television and performance through historical, theoretical and social perspectives. Students develop cultural criticism, research and cultural-sector practice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR programmes offer related routes through arts and media, culture and power, or literature and communication. Radboud provides more dedicated music and performance study, festival production and a separate bachelor thesis. The comparison uses Radboud’s currently published indicative plan for students starting in 2027.

curriculum.limitation: Radboud describes these 2027–2030 course offerings as indicative and subject to change. This planning comparison does not guarantee future courses or replace the applicable programme regulations.
